holidays.name: World Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day for unwrapping, melting, dunking and savoring everything cocoa. Bonbons, brownies, hot cocoa and the humble candy bar all get their moment in the spotlight, and fair-trade chocolate is a popular way to celebrate.
holidays.origin: Often linked to the story that chocolate first reached Europe in 1550, this observance has grown into a worldwide excuse to celebrate the sweet treat.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate comes from cacao beans, which ancient Mesoamericans enjoyed as a bitter, frothy drink long before anyone thought of sweet candy bars.

holidays.name: Global Forgiveness Day
holidays.description: A day set aside for letting go of grudges, mending fences and sending that long-overdue apology text. It encourages people to release old hurts and make peace with others and with themselves.
holidays.origin: The observance began in Canada and has since spread around the world as a call for reconciliation and kindness.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study forgiveness have linked it to lower stress and better emotional well-being, so the day may be good for your health too.

holidays.name: International Macaroni Day
holidays.description: A cheesy, carb-loaded tribute to the elbow-shaped pasta that has fed college students, picky kids and comfort-food lovers for generations. Baked, stovetop or straight from the blue box, all macaroni is welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, passed along by pasta fans who needed a reason to put a pot of water on to boil.
holidays.funFact: Thomas Jefferson is famously associated with introducing macaroni and cheese to American tables after encountering pasta in Europe.
